method: Read-only independent source, protocol, actual result and identity review; no maintained edits, expensive suite reruns or supplied ZIP media copies.
findings: Presentation only adds Admission.Contract to the existing observation. Room/Plan remain authoritative for accepted game consequences; audio adds no damage, payment, turn, result or alternate gameplay owner.

Admission is an engine-independent C#8/netstandard2.1 library using standard read-only collections. Its 13 ordered live states and three incoming ranks export 39 finite decisions consumed by the browser. The adapter does not reimplement the rank-selection algorithm or install a noncausal offline optimizer.

Two-voice admission preserves stronger playing consequences, replaces a weaker voice or threat peer, and explicitly suppresses saturated critical peers without a queue. Browser replacement and logical expiry disconnect the old node before appending; stale onended callbacks check both generation and live membership.

Mute, suspended observation, repeated/stale observation and explicit resume retain cursor ownership. Enable checks its epoch after asynchronous resume and decode; suspension and restart invalidate the generation. Reconnect requires explicit re-enable. A second narrow independent lifecycle review found no concrete blocker.

Ducking recomputes the greatest admitted end after start, suppression and completion; a later short cue cannot schedule release before a longer retained terminal voice. Existing aligned stem startup and mute controls remain intact.

The source sample bound is 0.45386993498348416 at maximum permitted bus gains, using a Euclidean bound for equal-power stems and two greatest cue peaks under master 0.8. Browser separately checks actual decoded peaks before playback; current decoded bound is approximately 0.454013 below 0.9. This is finite-source sample headroom, not a generic limiter.

Actual terminal/begin/action commands succeeded within the 0.60-second terminal lifetime. Music-zero final AudioContext capture retains a terminal-only late interval: 6175 frames, RMS 0.019062312820166037, nominal capture peak 0.19915173947811127. The forced-FIFO mutation kept game commands successful, recorded the critical stop and failed the same criterion with 6174 late frames at RMS zero.

The other controlled negatives are actual browser graph changes: isolated 37ms stem capture delay and master gain12. Their phase and over-range float PCM observations are distinct from errors, static metadata or fabricated result edits.

The separate supplied candidate has five passing builds but two failing runtime suites. Current records retain failure locations and do not imply whole-candidate/R32 adoption, Desktop execution or passing all validation.

result_accounting.research_record: 112 Python tests / 13 reproduced reports / 12-claim traceability / 48 held media are separately recorded intake observations; this final review does not claim to have rerun them.

limits: ScriptProcessor block playbackTime is a browser signal-clock proxy. Tail energy plus voice ownership is narrower than calibrated duration or full sample-by-sample continuity of the complete terminal cue.

No certified ITU true peak/LUFS, physical clipping, hardware latency/output, masking, recognition, comfort, preference, artistic approval or human validation is established. The supplied generic 4x estimate must retain this distinction.
Finite overload intentionally suppresses cues; consumption does not mean every consequence was heard. A new terminal arrival deliberately clears prior cues as documented.
Repeated explicit Enable restarts both aligned stems; this behavior predates the change and is not evidence of continuous transport across re-enable.
No Unity Editor, Windows Player, Steam, ordinary-user device or distribution-rights acceptance. All 48 supplied media remain held; current runtime uses only its ten unchanged original Composer WAVs.

This is agent review of the selected changes, not independent human/scientific validation or final repository publication approval. Primary still owns final manifests, gates, exact staged inventory, reconciliation and publication.
